intro_notes: NOTE: If collecting is permitted, do so ethically and sustainably. Collect sparingly, only taking what you need, and ensure that your collection practices do not harm the surrounding environment. Be aware of and adhere to local laws regarding collection. NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.req_text: Life Cycles. Do the following: (a) Compare the life histories of a butterfly and a grasshopper. Tell how they are different. (b) Raise an insect through complete metamorphosis from its larval stage to its adult stage (e.g., raise a butterfly or moth from a caterpillar). (Some insects are endangered species and are protected by federal or state law. Every species is found only in its own special type of habitat. Be sure to check natural resources authorities in advance to be sure that you will not be collecting any species that is known to be protected or endangered, or in any habitat where collecting is prohibited. In most cases, all specimens should be returned at the location of capture after the requirement has been met. Check with your counselor for those instances where the return of these specimens would not be appropriate.)

requirements.req_text: Observation and Analysis. Do the following: (a) Discuss the importance of the Leave No Trace Seven Principles and the Outdoor Code as they relate to insect study. Explain how you have followed the Leave No Trace Seven Principles and the Outdoor Code during field observation, specimen collection, and identification. (b) Observe 20 different live species of insects in their habitat. In your observations, include at least four orders of insects. (c) Make a scrapbook of the 20 insects you observe in 4(b). Include photographs, sketches, illustrations, and articles. Label each insect with its common and scientific names, where possible. Share your scrapbook with your counselor.Resources: How To Start a Bug Collection (video) How To Make an Insect Collection: Spreading (video) Collecting Insects: Tools and Supplies (video) Insect Collecting—Tools & Tips (video) (d) From your scrapbook collection, select eight species of insects and identify what role they play in the ecosystem.

Core Standard 1 (Req 8): Do the following: (a) Tell the migration route of an insect (e.g., monarch butterfly).
Core Standard 2 (Req 8): Discuss the challenges they face and how Scouts can contribute to their success.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 8): Review the official Insect Study requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing Conservation. Do the following: (a) Tell the migration.
Execute & Document: Perform the conservation task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Insect Study Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

Research the prospects for employment, starting salary, advancement opportunities and career goals associated with this career. Discuss what you learned with your counselor and whether you might be interested in this career.
